Rahman: Arabic, 'merciful' or 'compassionate'. Ar-Rahman is one of the names of God in Islam; commonly used in compounds such as Abdurrahman.
Angéline: French, a diminutive of Angèle, from Latin angelus, from Greek angelos 'messenger'.
Elmedin: Bosnian, from Arabic 'ilm 'knowledge' with din 'religion'; roughly 'knowledge of the faith'. Probably a variant of Alemdin.
Eléonor: French form of Eleanor, an Old Occitan name of uncertain origin, possibly linked to Helen. Made famous by Eleanor of Aquitaine.
Emran: Arabic Imran, the biblical Amram, father of Moses and of Mary in the Quran. Meaning often given as 'prosperous' or 'long-lived'.
Fantine: French, a diminutive of Fanny or Fantina, from Latin infans 'child'. Popularised by Victor Hugo's Les Misérables.
Ilkay: Turkish, from il 'country' or ilk 'first' with ay 'moon'; roughly 'first moon' or 'new moon'.
Irfan: Arabic, 'knowledge' or 'awareness', also used for spiritual insight in Sufism.
Juta: Probably a Baltic or Germanic variant of Jutta, itself a form of Judith, Hebrew for 'woman of Judea' or 'praised'.
Lennon: Irish surname Ó Leannáin, meaning 'descendant of Leannán' ('lover' or 'sweetheart'). Popularised by musician John Lennon.
Pacôme: French form of Pachomius, from Coptic, probably 'the eagle' or 'falcon'. Saint Pachomius founded Christian monasticism in Egypt.
Ramadan: Arabic, the ninth month of the Islamic calendar, from a root meaning 'scorching heat'. Used as a given name among Muslims.
Conner: Anglicised form of Irish Conchobhar, usually explained as 'lover of hounds' or 'wolf lover'. Variant of Connor.
Elvin: English, from Old English Ælfwine, 'elf friend'. Also used in Turkic and Azerbaijani settings.
Jayda: Modern English coinage, probably a variant of Jada or Jaida; possibly from Spanish jade or Arabic 'jayyida' ('excellent'). Origin uncertain.
Kaitlyn: English form of Caitlin, the Irish form of Catherine, from Greek, probably 'pure'.
Leopold: Germanic, from leud 'people' and bald 'bold'. Borne by Belgian kings; Leopold I was the first king of the Belgians.
Marceline: French feminine diminutive of Marcel, from Latin Marcellus, a diminutive of Marcus, possibly 'of Mars'.
Marek: Slavic form of Mark, from Latin Marcus, probably linked to the god Mars.
Maylie: Modern English-style coinage, probably a variant of Mailie or Mayleigh, blending May with Lee. Origin uncertain.
Savio: Italian, from Latin sapius, 'wise'. Associated with Saint Dominic Savio.
Tilde: Short form of Matilda, from Germanic maht 'might' and hild 'battle'. Common in Scandinavia.
Travis: English surname from Old French traveis, 'to cross' or a toll-gatherer at a crossing. Used as a given name since the 20th century.
Artan: Albanian, probably from art 'gold', hence 'golden'. Also found in Kosovo and Albania.
Chahinez: Arabic-Maghrebi, from Persian shahin, 'falcon' or 'royal hawk'. Variant spelling of Shahinaz.
Ebrar: Turkish form of Arabic abrar, 'the righteous' or 'pious ones'.
Faigy: Yiddish, from Faige or Feigl, 'little bird', from Yiddish foygl.
Nikolaos: Greek form of Nicholas, from nike 'victory' and laos 'people'.
Sevde: Turkish form of Arabic Sawda, 'black' or 'dark'; also linked to Turkish sevda 'love, passion'.
Shlomo: Hebrew form of Solomon, from shalom 'peace'.
Thijmen: Dutch variant of Thijmen, a form of Timon or Timotheus, from Greek 'honouring God'. Probably a Dutch spelling variant of Tijmen.
Timea: Hungarian, from Greek Timaia, 'honour' or 'valuable'. Probably derived from timē.
Yago: Galician and Spanish form of Iago, a variant of Jacob or Santiago, from Hebrew Yaakov, 'supplanter'.
Eloane: Modern French coinage, probably a blend of Eloïse or Eloi with Loane. Origin uncertain.
Elton: English place-name surname from Old English meaning 'Ella's settlement'. Also used in Albanian settings.
Erion: Albanian, perhaps from Greek erion 'wool', or a modern coinage. Origin uncertain.
Ronja: Scandinavian, created by Astrid Lindgren for Ronia the Robber's Daughter (1981). Likely coined from the Swedish place name Ronja.
Shirine: Persian Shirin, 'sweet'. Heroine of the Persian romance Khosrow and Shirin.
Alies: Dutch variant of Alice, from Old French Aalis, a short form of Adalheidis, 'noble kind'.
Naz: Persian and Turkish, 'grace', 'coquetry' or 'pride'. Also a short form of names like Nazlı.
Ness: Short form of Agnes (Greek 'pure') or Vanessa. Also a Scottish name from a loch and river.
Ninthe: Rare Dutch form, probably a variant of Ninte or Ninette, ultimately linked to Anne or Nina. Origin uncertain.
Adan: Spanish form of Adam, from Hebrew adamah 'earth'. Also an Arabic name, 'Aden'.
Bentley: English place-name surname from Old English beonet 'bent grass' and leah 'clearing'.
Betty: English diminutive of Elizabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Dayan: Hebrew, 'judge'. Also used in Turkic and Arabic settings with other meanings.
Gaïa: Greek Gaia, 'earth', the personification of the Earth in Greek mythology.
Josh: Short form of Joshua, from Hebrew Yehoshua, 'God is salvation'.
Klaudia: Polish, Czech, German and Slovak form of Claudia, from Latin claudius, 'lame' or 'limping'.
Maëlly: Modern French coinage, a variant of Maëlle or Maëlys, from Breton mael 'prince' or 'chief'.
Melia: Greek meliai, 'ash tree nymphs'. Also a variant of Amelia or Melia in Hawaiian settings.
Noussayba: Arabic Nusayba or Nusaybah, a diminutive of nasab 'lineage'. Borne by a female companion of the Prophet.
Sohayb: Arabic Suhayb, probably 'reddish' or 'red-haired'. Borne by Suhayb al-Rumi, a companion of Muhammad.
Winston: English, from the place Wynnstan, Old English wynn 'joy' and stan 'stone'. Made famous by Churchill.
Ani: Armenian, from the medieval capital city of Ani. Also a short form in Georgian and Hebrew settings.
Anna-Lucia: Compound of Anna (Hebrew 'grace') and Lucia (Latin lux, 'light').
Delya: Probably a variant of Delia, from Delos, the Greek island birthplace of Artemis; or a modern coined name. Origin uncertain.
Djayden: Modern spelling of Jayden, an American coinage, possibly from Hebrew Jadon, 'thankful' or 'he judged'. Origin uncertain.
Ilir: Albanian, 'Illyrian', after the ancient Illyrian people.
Konstantin: Slavic and German form of Constantine, from Latin constans, 'steadfast'.
Linoa: Probably a modern coined name, possibly related to Lino or Linnea. Origin uncertain.
Merveille: French, 'marvel' or 'wonder', from Latin mirabilia. Used as a given name especially in francophone Africa.
Mostafa: Persian and Arabic Mustafa, 'chosen' or 'selected', an epithet of the Prophet Muhammad.
Pinchas: Hebrew Phinehas, possibly from Egyptian 'the Nubian' or 'dark-skinned'. Biblical grandson of Aaron.
Angélina: French and Spanish diminutive of Angela, from Greek angelos, 'messenger'.
Avril: French, 'April', from Latin aprilis. Also an English given name via French.
Beren: Sindarin name in Tolkien's work meaning 'bold' or 'brave'. Also a Turkish name and a Germanic variant of 'bear'.
Danya: Slavic and Hebrew; a short form of Daniel, 'God is my judge', or a Russian diminutive of Daniil.
Ervin: English and Hungarian, from Old English Eoforwine, 'boar friend'. Also a Hungarian form of Irwin.
Erza: Albanian and Hebrew; Albanian name possibly from Ezra, Hebrew 'help'. Origin uncertain.
Hani: Arabic, 'content' or 'happy'. Also a Japanese name with various meanings.
Sayfullah: Arabic, 'sword of God', an epithet of the general Khalid ibn al-Walid.
Sonya: Russian diminutive of Sofia, from Greek sophia, 'wisdom'.
Asa: Hebrew, 'healer' or 'physician'. Biblical king of Judah. Also Japanese and Scandinavian use.
Aslihan: Turkish Aslıhan, from asıl 'noble' or 'original' and han 'ruler' or 'khan'. Probably 'noble lady'.
Charlene: English feminine of Charles, from Germanic karl, 'free man'.
Hermione: Greek, feminine of Hermes, perhaps 'earthly' or 'of Hermes'. Daughter of Helen and Menelaus in myth; also a Harry Potter heroine.
Mayssam: Arabic Maysam, from maysam 'beautiful face' or 'smiling'. Variant spelling of Maysam.
Moishe: Yiddish form of Moses, from Hebrew Moshe, probably Egyptian 'son' or Hebrew 'drawn out'.
Mordechai: Hebrew, possibly from Babylonian Marduk. Biblical cousin of Esther in the Book of Esther.
Romano: Italian and Spanish, 'Roman', from Latin romanus. Also a Romani word for 'Romani'.
Seline: Variant of Selina or Céline, from Latin caelum 'heaven' or Greek selene 'moon'.
Sura: Arabic sura, 'chapter of the Quran'. Also a Hebrew name, 'turn aside', and a Slavic name.
Adina: Hebrew, 'delicate' or 'gentle'. Also a Romanian name, probably related to Adèle.
Elmira: Probably a variant of Almira, from Arabic amira 'princess'. Also used in Tatar and Kazakh.
Eryn: Welsh and English; Welsh eryn possibly 'eagle', and Tolkien used it for 'forest'. Variant of Erin 'Ireland'.
Avi: Hebrew, 'my father', often a short form of Avraham or Avigail.
Era: Probably modern Albanian or English use; Albanian era means 'wind'. Also English 'era'. Origin uncertain.
Eythan: Variant spelling of Ethan, from Hebrew eitan, 'strong' or 'firm'.
Inass: Arabic Ines, a variant of Inas or Anas, 'sociability' or 'companionship'. Also a French spelling of Inès.
Neila: Probably a variant of Nelly or Neil, from Gaelic Niall 'champion' or 'cloud'. In Arabic, Nayla means 'achieving'.
Amra: Bosnian and Arabic; possibly from Arabic amra 'princess' or 'commander'. Origin uncertain.
Auréline: French, from Latin aurum 'gold', variant of Aurélie.
Christiano: Italian and Portuguese form of Christian, from Greek Christos, 'anointed'.
Iker: Basque, 'visitation', referring to the Virgin Mary's visit to Elizabeth.
Joya: Spanish and Italian 'jewel' or Hindi 'joy'. Probably from Latin gaudia.
Julyan: Variant of Julian, from Latin Julianus, 'belonging to Julius' (family of Julius Caesar).
Kailey: Modern English; probably a variant of Kaylee or Kayleigh, a coined blend. Origin uncertain.
Levin: Dutch and German from Old English leof 'dear' and wine 'friend'; also a form of Hebrew Levi.
Lylian: Modern coined name, perhaps a blend of Lily and Lian. Origin uncertain.
Maure: French form of Maurus, 'Moor' or 'dark-skinned', from Latin. Variant of Maurice.
Milow: Probably an anglicised form of Milo, from Germanic or Slavic mil 'dear' or 'gracious'; also the stage name of Belgian singer Milow.
Zackary: Variant of Zachary, from Hebrew Zekharyah, 'God remembers'.
Aissa: Arabic Aïssa, a form of Isa 'Jesus', or Aisha 'alive'. Also an Arabic short form.
Aristide: French and Italian, from Greek Aristides, 'son of the best', from aristos 'best'.
Don: Short form of Donald, from Gaelic Dòmhnall, 'world ruler'. Also Spanish 'sir'.
Enisa: Bosnian, from Arabic Anisa, 'friendly' or 'close companion'.
Guillermo: Spanish form of William, from Germanic wil 'will' and helm 'helmet'.
Iago: Spanish and Welsh form of Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov, 'supplanter'. Shakespeare's villain in Othello.
Marisa: Spanish and Italian, a combination of Maria and Luisa or from Latin maris 'of the sea'.
Maxandre: French blend of Max (from Maximilian, 'greatest') and Alexandre, 'defender of men'.
Moses: Hebrew Moshe, possibly from Egyptian 'son' or Hebrew 'to draw out'. Biblical leader of the Exodus.
Nuri: Arabic and Turkish, 'my light' or 'luminous', from nur 'light'.
Vin: Short form of Vincent, from Latin vincens, 'conquering'. Also a Dutch nickname.
Wanne: Dutch, a diminutive of Johanna or Wannes; Wannes is a Flemish short form of Johannes. Origin uncertain.
Yvonne: French, feminine of Yvon, from Germanic iv 'yew'. Probably 'archer'.
Aliza: Hebrew, 'joyful'. Also an Arabic and South Asian variant of Aliya.
Ebubekir: Turkish form of Abu Bakr, 'father of the young camel'. The first caliph of Islam.
Ellyn: Variant of Ellen, itself a form of Helen, from Greek helene, possibly 'torch'.
Emke: Frisian and Dutch, a diminutive of Emma or Emmanuel, from Germanic irmin 'whole' or Hebrew 'God with us'.
Esthée: French variant of Esther, from Persian 'star'. Also linked to the brand name Estée.
Gabriëlle: French feminine of Gabriel, Hebrew for 'God is my strength'.
Guilherme: Portuguese form of William, from Germanic wil 'will' and helm 'helmet'.
Jena: Probably a variant of Jenna or Jean; also a German city name. In Arabic Jenaan means 'gardens'. Origin uncertain.
Josefine: German, Dutch and Scandinavian feminine of Joseph, Hebrew for 'God will add'.
Keyan: Probably a variant of Kian, from Irish ciar 'dark', or a Persian 'king'. Origin uncertain.
Luïs: Portuguese and Spanish form of Louis, from Germanic hlud 'famous' and wig 'battle'.
Mehmed: Turkish and Bosnian form of Muhammad, Arabic for 'praised'.
Radia: Arabic Radiya, 'contented' or 'satisfied'. Also a Latin-derived form of radius.
Rafaela: Spanish, Portuguese and Czech feminine of Raphael, Hebrew for 'God has healed'.
Raffael: German and Italian form of Raphael, Hebrew for 'God has healed'. Archangel and painter.
Reyyan: Turkish, from Arabic rayyan, 'well-watered' or 'gate of Paradise'.
Siraç: Turkish form of Arabic siraj, 'lamp' or 'light'.
Farès: French form of Arabic Faris, 'knight' or 'horseman'.
Fiel: Probably a Dutch or Frisian short form of names like Fiele or Fidel, from Latin fidelis 'faithful'. Origin uncertain.
Kaï: Variant of Kai, a name from Frisian, Hawaiian ('sea') and Welsh traditions; possibly also from Greek.
Lokman: Arabic Luqman, 'wise man' in the Quran, a sage with his own chapter.
Melchior: Biblical, from Hebrew melekh 'king' and or 'light', 'king of light'. Traditional name of one of the three Magi.
Tessio: Italian, probably a variant of Tessio or Tazio. Tessio is a character in The Godfather. Origin uncertain.
Xiebe: Rare Frisian or Dutch form, probably a variant of Siebe, from Germanic sigi 'victory' and bern 'bear'. Uncertain.
Aminah: Arabic Amina, 'trustworthy' or 'faithful'. Mother of the Prophet Muhammad.
Blanka: Slavic and Hungarian form of Blanche, from Germanic blank 'white' or 'shining'.
Daris: Probably a variant of Darius, from Persian Dārayavahush, 'holding firm the good'. Origin uncertain.
Frieda: German, from Old High German fridu 'peace'. Short form of names like Elfrieda.
Heyden: English and Dutch place-name surname, from heyden 'heath'. Modern given name.
Iseult: Celtic legend heroine, from Old Welsh Essyllt, perhaps 'she who is gazed at'. Tristan and Iseult.
Kuba: Polish short form of Jakub, the Polish form of Jacob, from Hebrew Yaakov, 'supplanter'.
Mani: Persian prophet name Mani, founder of Manichaeism. Also Sanskrit 'jewel' and Arabic 'determined'.
Maxima: Latin, 'greatest', feminine of Maximus. Used by the Dutch queen Máxima.
Nourhane: Arabic Nourhan, from nur 'light' with the suffix -an. Roughly 'light'.
Serine: Probably a variant of Serena or Sirine, from Latin serenus 'clear' or Arabic. Origin uncertain.
Silvana: Italian feminine of Silvano, from Latin silva 'forest'.
Djulian: Phonetic spelling of Julian, from Latin Julianus, 'belonging to Julius'.
Fik: Dutch short form of Frederik, from Germanic fridu 'peace' and ric 'ruler'. Possibly a nickname.
Flinn: Anglicised form of Irish Flann, 'red' or 'ruddy'. Also Irish surname Ó Floinn.
Ilyess: Arabic Ilyas, form of Elijah, from Hebrew Eliyahu, 'my God is Yahweh'.
Iulia: Romanian form of Julia, feminine of Latin Julius, of uncertain origin.
Kirill: Russian form of Cyril, from Greek kyrios, 'lord'.
Leanne: English, a blend of Lee and Anne, or from Gaelic. Probably Hebrew 'grace'.
Marloes: Dutch, a contraction of Maria and Loes (Louise). Maria is Hebrew in origin.
Mihrimah: Turkish, from Persian mihr 'sun' and mah 'moon'. Daughter of Suleiman the Magnificent.
Rayaan: Arabic Rayyan, 'well-watered' or 'luxuriant'; the Rayyan gate of Paradise.
Ridwan: Arabic Ridwan, 'good pleasure' or 'approval'. The guardian of Paradise.
Suna: Turkish, 'drake' or 'male duck'; also Turkic 'beautiful' and Scandinavian. Origin varies.
Thobias: Scandinavian and Dutch form of Tobias, Hebrew 'God is good'.
Vico: Italian, probably a short form of Ludovico or Enrico. Also 'neighbourhood' in Latin.
Abdurahman: Arabic, 'servant of the Merciful', from abd 'servant' and al-Rahman.
Elyes: North African French form of Ilyas, Arabic for Elijah, Hebrew 'my God is Yahweh'.
Fen: English fen 'marsh'; also a Chinese name 'fragrance'. Dutch short form possible.
Joas: Dutch form of Joash, Hebrew 'Yahweh has given'. Biblical king of Judah.
Mathy: Short form of Mathieu or Matthias, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Maylee: Modern English coinage blending May and Lee. Origin uncertain.
Tor: Scandinavian, 'Thor', Old Norse god of thunder. Also English 'rocky peak'.
Carina: Latin carina, 'keel', or Italian cara 'dear'. Also a constellation.
Cemre: Turkish, 'ember', and the heat that falls in turn on air, water and earth before spring.
Issrae: Arabic Israa, 'night journey', referring to the Prophet Muhammad's night journey.
Kayron: Modern coined name, perhaps linked to Cairon or Kieran 'dark'. Origin uncertain.
Neda: Persian and Slavic; Persian 'voice' or 'call', Slavic from nedelja 'Sunday'.
Sahel: Arabic, 'shore' or 'coast'. Also the Sahel region of Africa.
Abd: Arabic, 'servant' or 'slave', typically a prefix in compounds such as Abdullah.
Babet: French and Dutch diminutive of Elisabeth, Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Halim: Arabic, 'forbearing' or 'gentle'. One of the names of God.
